author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can cancel an upcoming visit from the owner's record
summary: An upcoming visit — one dated later than today — offers a cancel action on the owner detail page, and cancelling withdraws it from the pet's record. A visit dated today or earlier offers no action and a request to cancel it is refused.
acceptance_criteria: given a pet with a visit dated later than today, when the owner's record is opened, then that visit offers a cancel action
given a pet with a visit dated today or earlier, when the owner's record is opened, then that visit offers no cancel action
given an upcoming visit, when it is cancelled, then the owner's record is shown again without it, and the pet's visit history no longer lists it anywhere it is shown
given a pet with several visits, when one is cancelled, then the pet's other visits remain and no other pet's visits change

given a request to cancel a visit dated today or earlier, when it is submitted, then it is refused, that visit remains on the pet's record, and the staff member is told the cancellation was refused rather than seeing it confirmed
given a request to cancel a visit that does not exist, or one that does not belong to the named pet and owner, when it is submitted, then it is refused and no visit is withdrawn from any record
non_goals: amending a booked visit — changing its date, description, or pet (NG-11)
deleting an owner or a pet (NG-10)
cancelling a visit dated today or earlier
reversing a cancellation; rebooking is a new visit
filtering or reordering the visit table beyond what the cancel action needs
notes: Boundary decisions made in the PRD, not open: (1) upcoming means dated later than today — the same boundary REQ-VIS-001 applies to booking, so today's visits are NOT cancellable; (2) 'withdrawn from the pet's record' is stated as observable outcome only — whether that is a hard removal or a retained-but-hidden lifecycle state is a design decision, deliberately left to system-design; (3) refusals cover past visits, unknown visits, and visits not under the named pet and owner. NG-4 and NG-5 are retired to the Superseded list and replaced by NG-10 and NG-11; no ID was renumbered. REQ-LANG-002 makes the cancel action's label a translation obligation across all eleven message bundles — messages.properties is listed as a file target, the other ten follow. Two follow-ups outside my write scope: docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for 2026-08-06-non-goal-visit-amendment.md, and system-design.md will need the visit-cancellation mechanism section that REQ-VIS-003 defers. An open question is recorded in the PRD for booking mistakes noticed after the visit date; this slice does not depend on it.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Cancellation is genuinely new ground: it is the application's first destructive write path, and the mechanism the PRD refused to name is now decided as hard removal. Two durable-memory writes back this slice: docs/adr/2026-08-06-cancellation-removes-the-visit-row.md (the mechanism decision and the three rejected alternatives) and docs/system-design.md section Visit Cancellation, under Contracts after Persistence, anchored #visit-cancellation. Decision: the visit row is removed, not retained-but-hidden. Pet's visit association gains orphan removal; the cancel handler removes the visit from the owner aggregate loaded for the request and saves the owner through OwnerRepository. A lifecycle state was rejected because NG-11 leaves it a single reader (the code that would hide cancelled visits), it would cost a status column in three hand-maintained vendor schemas whose divergence already produced the MySQL known defect, and it would introduce the application's first lifecycle state against a codebase whose only state distinction is persisted-or-not. The State Machine section stays empty by that decision. Everything else fits existing shape: feature-package organization with no service layer (ADR 2026-07-31-feature-package-organization), rules in the controller, Owner as the sole write path for the owner-pet-visit graph.
integration_points: Route and method: POST on a cancel action segment under /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}, in VisitController. VisitController owns the /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/** sub-path already (booking is GET+POST on .../visits/new); OwnerController owns /owners/{ownerId} and /owners/{ownerId}/edit, PetController owns the pets sub-path. Splitting by URL sub-path is the existing convention, so cancellation stays in VisitController. POST not GET: the action changes stored data and no caller is authenticated, so a crawler or prefetch of a GET cancel URL would destroy visits. Not DELETE: no client-side layer exists and an HTML form issues GET or POST only; HiddenHttpMethodFilter is not enabled. The action segment (cancel) matches the existing new and edit action segments and keeps the ubiquitous-language term visible in the URL. ownerId stays in the path because the aggregate is entered through Owner.

Refusals surface through the existing flash-attribute convention: redirect to /owners/{ownerId} with addFlashAttribute("error", ...) for a refusal and addFlashAttribute("message", ...) for a completed cancellation. ownerDetails.html already renders both (#success-message and #error-message divs). This covers the two new refusals: visit not upcoming, and visit identifier naming no visit under the named pet and owner. A missing owner or a pet not held by that owner keeps surfacing through loadPetWithVisit's existing IllegalArgumentException path (error page), unchanged by this slice - there is no owner page to redirect to in that case.

The race in PRD edge case 5: the upcoming check belongs in the POST handler, evaluated against the visit's stored date at submit time. The render-time check on the owner detail page decides only whether to offer the action; it is presentation, not a control. The submitted request carries the visit identifier and no date - nothing the caller supplies may decide whether the visit is upcoming. This is also what closes the direct-POST hole, since no authentication exists and hiding the button is not a control.

One definition of the upcoming boundary, on Visit (an isUpcoming-style predicate reading its own date). REQ-VIS-001 booking and REQ-VIS-003 cancellation share the boundary by ADR 2026-08-06-non-goal-visit-amendment's own consequence note; a second inline expression would be free to drift. Booking's inline check in processNewVisitForm may adopt the same predicate in a TDD Refactor step - it is the same expression on the same field.

Visits table rendering: the cancel action is offered beside an upcoming visit only. A visit dated today or earlier renders an empty action cell. Not a disabled button (a visible control the reader cannot use, needing its own translated label) and not explanatory text (new vocabulary in eleven bundles that no acceptance criterion asks for). The table gains one action column with an untexted header cell, which carries no translation obligation. The existing trailing Edit Pet / Add Visit row stays as it is.

Visit location and ownership check are structural: walk owner -> getPet(petId) -> visit by id, from the Owner loaded for the request. No repository lookup keyed on a visit identifier. A visit under another owner's pet is simply not found, so the ownership refusal needs no separate hand-written check and cannot be forgotten.

REQ-LANG-002: the cancel action's label is a message key resolved in the template, added to messages.properties and to all ten locale bundles. I18nPropertiesSyncTest enforces both halves - checkNonInternationalizedStrings fails on a literal label in the HTML, checkI18nPropertyFilesAreInSync fails on a bundle missing the key (it skips messages_en.properties, which is empty by the English-fallback design; the key is still added to the other nine locales plus the base).

patterns.description: processNewVisitForm: the POST-check-flash-redirect shape the cancel handler mirrors, including the inline date rule and redirect:/owners/{ownerId}
Owner.addVisit(petId, visit): the aggregate-root entry point cancellation mirrors in the removal direction
Owner.getPet(Integer): null-returning lookup by identity within the aggregate; the visit lookup on Pet follows the same shape
the message and error flash-attribute alert divs the refusals and the confirmation render through

risks.risk: VisitController's @ModelAttribute("visit") loadPetWithVisit runs before EVERY handler in the controller, and it mutates the loaded Pet by calling pet.addVisit(new Visit()). A cancel handler that consumes that same Owner from the model and saves it would cascade-persist a blank transient Visit and fail on the @NotBlank description constraint.
risks.mitigation: Drop the pet.addVisit(visit) line from loadPetWithVisit so the shared model attribute is read-only. Behaviour is preserved: createOrUpdateVisitForm.html already filters unsaved visits out of the previous-visits list via th:if="${!visit['new']}", and processNewVisitForm adds the visit itself through owner.addVisit(petId, visit). Cover REQ-VIS-002 with a test before making the change. This is a two-line adjustment inside a file the slice already touches, foldable into a TDD Refactor step - not a refactor-first slice.

risks.risk: Orphan removal on Pet's visit association makes OwnerRepository.save authoritative over each pet's visit set. A save of a partially populated Owner would silently delete the visits absent from it.
risks.mitigation: Every existing write path already loads the Owner whole through OwnerRepository.findById with EAGER pets and visits (OwnerController.processUpdateOwnerForm, PetController.findOwner, VisitController.loadPetWithVisit), so no current path is affected. The invariant is recorded in system-design.md #visit-cancellation. A test that cancels one visit and asserts the pet's other visits and another pet's visits survive (the prd-entry's theCancellationShouldLeaveTheOtherVisitsOfThePetInPlace) pins it.

risks.risk: pet_id is nullable in all three vendor schemas. Without orphan removal, removing a Visit from the collection issues UPDATE visits SET pet_id = NULL, which satisfies the observable outcome by accident while leaving an undeletable orphan row.
risks.mitigation: orphanRemoval on the Pet-to-Visit association is required, not optional. An integration test against the real database (not a MockMvc-only test) must assert the row is gone rather than only that the page no longer lists it.

risks.risk: A cancel form nested inside the visits table on ownerDetails.html adds one form element per upcoming visit row. Nested forms are invalid HTML if the table ever sits inside another form.
risks.mitigation: ownerDetails.html carries no enclosing form today. Keep the per-row form as the innermost element of the action cell.

notes: Five-signal foundational check: none tripped. system-design.md is populated and partly confirmed, ADRs record the platform and architecture shape, ubiquitous-language.md already carries Upcoming Visit and Cancellation (both resolved 2026-08-06), and persistence, error-flow and configuration patterns are all recorded. No new bounded context. Not conflicting: ADR 2026-08-06-non-goal-visit-amendment explicitly leaves the mechanism open for this triage to settle. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is a no-op. Follow-up discharged: docs/adr/README.md now carries index rows for 2026-08-06-non-goal-visit-amendment.md and for the new 2026-08-06-cancellation-removes-the-visit-row.md. Follow-up remaining for product-requirements-expert: the PRD's Visits section carries an **ADR:** line but no **Design:** link - it should read **Design:** [system-design.md#visit-cancellation](system-design.md#visit-cancellation), matching the Pets and Veterinarian sections. Flash-message wording: the new confirmation and refusal strings stay hard-coded English literals in the controller, matching every existing flash string ("Your visit has been booked", "New Owner Created", "There was an error in creating the owner"). REQ-LANG-002's acceptance bullet is page-scoped ("no user-facing text is hard-coded into a page") and I18nPropertiesSyncTest checks .html files only, so this slice is consistent with the requirement as written and as enforced. Translating flash text would put two conventions in the same alert box on the same page. Whether controller-authored flash wording falls under REQ-LANG-002 is a repo-wide question for product-requirements-expert, not something to half-fix here.

Three implementation decisions beyond what the line-4 block specified, all affirmed. (2) pet.addVisit(visit) was dropped from loadPetWithVisit - that @ModelAttribute method runs for every mapping in the controller including the cancel POST, so with orphan removal in place a save of the loaded owner would cascade-persist a blank form-backing visit. patterns.description: aggregate traversal mirroring the existing getPet(Integer)/addVisit(petId, visit) pair; ownership refusal falls out of the walk rather than being a check that can be forgotten

risks.risk: No CSRF protection and no authentication exist anywhere in the application, and cancellation is its first destructive POST. A cross-site form post can now delete an upcoming visit, where previously the worst outcome was a spurious booking.

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: The aggregate walk (Owner.getVisit -> Owner.getPet -> Pet.getVisit) is the ONLY access control on the application's first destructive endpoint, under a confirmed no-authentication posture (docs/system-design.md Security Context). Its cross-owner arm is unpinned. Every cancel test uses TEST_OWNER_ID = 1 and a single mocked owners.findById(1); theCancellationOfAVisitNotBelongingToTheNamedPetShouldBeRefused only covers a sibling pet UNDER THE SAME OWNER (TEST_OTHER_PET_ID = 2 on this.owner). The cross-owner arm is a different code path: for POST /owners/1/pets/{petId of another owner}/visits/{visitId}/cancel, loadPetWithVisit throws IllegalArgumentException before processCancelVisitForm ever runs, and for an unknown ownerId it throws on the orElseThrow. I traced both and they are structurally safe today - Owner.getPets is join-column scoped to owner_id, so another owner's pet is absent from the list and getPet returns null; Pet.getVisit only scans that pet's visits, so a foreign visit id is unreachable. The gap is regression cover, not a live defect: nothing fails the build if a future refactor replaces the walk with a visit-id lookup or moves the owner load. REQ-VIS-003 acceptance criterion 6 names this case explicitly ('does not belong to the named pet and owner ... no visit is withdrawn from any record').
findings.fix: Add two cases to VisitControllerTests. (1) theCancellationOfAVisitBelongingToAnotherOwnersPetShouldBeRefused: stub a second owner (given(owners.findById(TEST_OTHER_OWNER_ID)) with its own pet and upcoming visit), POST /owners/{TEST_OWNER_ID}/pets/{TEST_PET_ID}/visits/{other owner's visit id}/cancel, assert the refusal (flash 'error', redirect) and verify(owners, never()).save(any(Owner.class)) plus that the other owner's visit set is untouched. (2) theCancellationUnderAnOwnerThatDoesNotHoldThePetShouldNotWithdrawAnyVisit: POST with a petId held by the second owner against TEST_OWNER_ID and assert no save reaches the repository. Both belong in the class-exhaustive sweep of the same authorization-boundary class.

findings.description: theCancellationShouldNotLetTheRequestChangeTheOwnersDetails pins the mass-assignment guard on @ModelAttribute(binding = false) with top-level scalar params only (firstName, city). I verified the guard itself is correct: Spring's ModelAttributeMethodProcessor skips bindRequestParameters entirely when binding = false, the attribute name resolves to 'owner' matching loadPetWithVisit's model.put("owner", owner), and no other bindable @ModelAttribute parameter exists on the cancel handler - so POST ...cancel?firstName=Intruder cannot rewrite the owner. The test is sound as far as it goes. What it does not pin is the nested arm the design-block at line 8 named as the sibling defect's blast radius: pets[n] fields, reachable because Owner.getPets hands out the live list. A future edit that drops binding = false (or narrows it to a disallowed-field list, the weaker pattern the other handlers use) would still pass this test while re-opening the nested vector on the destructive path.
findings.fix: Extend the existing test with .param("pets[0].name", "Intruder") and assert this.pet.getName() is unchanged, alongside the current firstName/city assertions. One extra param and one assertion in the test already present - no new test method needed.

approved_aspects: Authorization-by-aggregate holds on every path I traced. Owner.getVisit(petId, visitId) resolves through Owner.getPet (scoped by the owner_id join column) then Pet.getVisit (scoped by the pet_id join column), so a visit under another owner's pet is structurally unreachable rather than filtered by a check that can be forgotten. No visit-id-keyed lookup exists anywhere: there is no VisitRepository, and the handler never queries by visitId alone. IDOR is closed by construction.

Refusal paths leak nothing. The not-found refusal and the cross-owner refusal produce the identical flash string ('That visit was not found and has not been cancelled'), so the endpoint is not an existence oracle for visit ids. No exception message, stack trace, or identifier reaches the reader on these paths. The unknown-owner and foreign-pet cases surface through loadPetWithVisit's pre-existing IllegalArgumentException, and server.error.include-message is left at the Spring Boot default of 'never' (no override in src/main/resources/application*.properties), so the interpolated ids in those messages do not render.

The upcoming boundary is enforced server-side against the STORED date via Visit.isUpcoming(), never against anything the request carries - the request supplies only path identifiers. The render-time judgment in ownerDetails.html is presentation only; removing the th:if from the page cannot make a past visit cancellable. Booking now shares the single definition, so the two cannot drift apart.

orphanRemoval = true introduces no cascade beyond the cancelled visit. I traced every OwnerRepository.save/saveAndFlush call site: VisitController (both handlers), OwnerController.processCreationForm and processUpdateOwnerForm, PetController.processCreationForm and updatePetDetails. Each saves an Owner obtained from findById with Owner.pets and Pet.visits both EAGER - i.e. loaded whole - or a brand-new Owner with no pets. updatePetDetails mutates the existing Pet in place rather than replacing it, leaving its visit set intact. Form binding cannot shrink the set either: Pet.visits is a LinkedHashSet behind a final field, and Spring's BeanWrapper supports indexed access and auto-grow on List/array/Map only, so no visits[n] path is bindable. Dropping pet.addVisit(visit) from loadPetWithVisit correctly closes the one new cascade-persist hazard the change would otherwise have created, and it is guarded by theNewVisitFormShouldNotAddAnUnsavedVisitToThePetsRecord.

No injection surface added. The new JdbcTemplate helpers in ClinicServiceTests use bound ? placeholders with no string concatenation; all production data access remains Spring Data derived queries. The new template cell renders through th:text and builds the form action with the named-parameter URL expression @{/owners/{ownerId}/.../cancel(ownerId=...,petId=...,visitId=...)}, which URL-encodes its arguments - notably avoiding the __${...}__ preprocessing form used elsewhere in the same file. Thymeleaf auto-escaping is not disabled anywhere; no th:utext exists in the templates. The three new flash strings are compile-time constants rendered through th:text into the pre-existing message/error divs.
No secrets in the diff. The full change set contains no credential, token, key, or connection-string literal; the only new resource values are the eleven cancelVisit translations.
Supply chain unchanged: build.gradle, pom.xml, and the lockfiles are absent from scripts/changeset.sh --name-only, so this slice adds no dependency and no version delta. No new CVE surface to assess.

CSRF and the absent authentication were verified as recorded-and-deferred, not re-litigated. The design-block at line 8 states the position, the risk is carried in docs/system-design.md Security Context and the Threat Model's first row, and POST-only was chosen deliberately so a prefetch cannot cancel. I confirmed the consequence is real - a cross-site form post can now delete an upcoming visit where the prior worst case was a spurious booking - and I agree a filter chain touching every mutating route does not belong inside this slice. The pre-existing processNewVisitForm mass assignment is likewise accepted as deferred; its Known Defects row in docs/system-design.md is accurate, including the pets[n] blast radius, and the cancel handler is correctly unaffected.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can cancel an upcoming visit from the owner's record
summary: An upcoming visit — one dated later than today — offers a cancel action on the owner detail page, and cancelling withdraws it from the pet's record. A visit dated today or earlier offers no action and a request to cancel it is refused.
acceptance_criteria: given a pet with a visit dated later than today, when the owner's record is opened, then that visit offers a cancel action
given a pet with a visit dated today or earlier, when the owner's record is opened, then that visit offers no cancel action
given an upcoming visit, when it is cancelled, then the owner's record is shown again without it, and the pet's visit history no longer lists it anywhere it is shown
given a pet with several visits, when one is cancelled, then the pet's other visits remain and no other pet's visits change

given a request to cancel a visit dated today or earlier, when it is submitted, then it is refused, that visit remains on the pet's record, and the staff member is told the cancellation was refused rather than seeing it confirmed
given a request to cancel a visit that does not exist, or one that does not belong to the named pet and owner, when it is submitted, then it is refused and no visit is withdrawn from any record
non_goals: amending a booked visit — changing its date, description, or pet (NG-11)
deleting an owner or a pet (NG-10)
cancelling a visit dated today or earlier
reversing a cancellation; rebooking is a new visit
filtering or reordering the visit table beyond what the cancel action needs

approved_aspects: Round-1 finding 1 (cross-owner arm unpinned) is closed. theCancellationOfAVisitBelongingToAnotherOwnersPetShouldBeRefused POSTs visit id 13 (held by a second owner's pet 3) under TEST_OWNER_ID with petId=TEST_PET_ID; the walk in Owner.getVisit returns null, so the test asserts the refusal flash, verify(owners, never()).save(any(Owner.class)), and the foreign visit set intact. Round-1 finding 1, second arm: theCancellationUnderAnOwnerThatDoesNotHoldThePetShouldNotWithdrawAnyVisit pins the pre-handler refusal. VisitController.loadPetWithVisit throws IllegalArgumentException when owner.getPet(petId) is null, and MockMvc surfaces it wrapped as ServletException. Pinning the wrapper type is acceptable here because the assertion is fail-closed: if a refactor moved the owner load and let the request through, assertThatExceptionOfType(...).isThrownBy(...) fails rather than passing vacuously, and the no-save plus foreign-visit-set-intact assertions carry the actual security invariant independently of the wrapping. findings.description: This test pins jakarta.servlet.ServletException as the outer thrown type, with IllegalArgumentException only as the root cause. No other test in the suite asserts on MockMvc's servlet-exception wrapping (CrashControllerTests calls the controller method directly rather than through MockMvc, so it never sees the wrapper). The outer ServletException is an artifact of MockMvc dispatch/Spring's uncaught-exception plumbing, not application behavior; the observable claim the test title makes ("should not withdraw any visit") is fully carried by the two assertions that already follow it (otherOwnersPet visits unchanged, save never called). Given the app has no @ExceptionHandler (confirmed: none exists in src/main), pinning some outer exception type is likely unavoidable with MockMvc, so this is not blocking - but the exact outer-type pin adds a coupling to transport plumbing that a Spring upgrade could legitimately change without the underlying refusal behavior changing at all.
findings.fix: Optional: relax the outer type to assertThatExceptionOfType(Exception.class) so the assertion states only what matters - some exception propagates with IllegalArgumentException as its root cause - without pinning Spring's specific wrapper type.

author: change-grader
summary: cancel an upcoming visit from the owner detail page

blast_radius.note: Reaches past the new handler in three ways. orphanRemoval=true on Pet.visits is a global mapping change: every Owner save is now authoritative over each pet's visit set, so any save path holding a truncated graph would silently delete rows. I traced all five save paths (OwnerController create and edit, PetController create and edit, VisitController book and cancel) and each loads the owner whole through the EAGER graph, so none truncates today, but the invariant is now load-bearing and lives only in a Javadoc. loadPetWithVisit lost its pet.addVisit(visit), and that method runs before every handler in VisitController, so the pre-existing booking path changed too. And this is the application's first destructive POST on a confirmed no-authentication, no-CSRF codebase, so any cross-site form can withdraw a visit with no token.

semantic_surprise.note: The code hides nothing and reads cleanly: isUpcoming() is exactly equivalent to the booking check it replaced (both guarded on a non-null date), the ownership walk really is structural, and the cancel handler judges the boundary against the stored date rather than anything the request carries. The surprise is the one thing reading cannot settle. Production loads the owner in loadPetWithVisit outside any transaction with open-in-view disabled and no @Transactional in the controller, so owners.save(owner) is a merge of a detached parent. Orphan removal through merge is subtler than the cascade-persist-through-merge the booking path already relies on, and if it fails to fire the failure is exactly the one the ADR was written to prevent: UPDATE visits SET pet_id = NULL, an orphan row, invisible on the page and green in every test.

test_adequacy.note: The suite is real, not tautological: 598 test lines against 128 production lines, JdbcTemplate row counts rather than in-memory assertions, containsExactly on visit ids, verify(never()).save on every refusal arm, both sides of the today boundary, cross-pet and cross-owner negative arms, a mass-assignment pin proving the request cannot reach the loaded owner, and a regression pin that booking still lists earlier visits. One seam is open. The controller tests mock OwnerRepository, so they prove save was called, never that a row died; the only real-database proof lives in ClinicServiceTests, which is @DataJpaTest and @Transactional and therefore operates on a managed entity. Nothing joins the two ends, so the detached-merge path the controller actually uses is exercised by no test.

reviewer_hedging.note: Not a clean unanimous close. Round 1 had three of four reviewers request changes; round 2 approved across the full roster, but the test-reviewer's approval carries a finding it chose not to require, on the ServletException outer-type pin coupling a test to MockMvc transport plumbing. That one is a nit and should not be over-weighted. The substantive hedge sits behind the security approval: the CSRF exposure on this endpoint was accepted as pre-existing NG-1 posture rather than resolved, with the design owner recording that a first destructive POST makes that posture worse in consequence. Approval there means the risk was priced, not removed.

scope_deviation.note: The diff itself stayed inside REQ-VIS-003. Every production hunk either serves cancellation or is forced by it, and the doc churn is the requirement's own paperwork. What warrants a signature is where the scope came from. The slice retired two standing non-goals, NG-4 and NG-5, minting NG-10 and NG-11 to carry the residue, and the log records consultations: 0, so no human was asked. The PRD's own preamble says whether any non-goal row was deliberately declined, deferred, or never considered remains part of an open consultation, and this slice retired two rows from that table anyway. design_revisions: 2 also shows the design was reworked twice before a line was written.

rationale: Unusually well documented and well tested, but the fact everything rests on, that cancelling deletes the row, is proven only against a managed entity inside a transaction while production merges a detached owner. Confirm orphan removal fires through save, then sign off on the non-goal reversal and the unguarded destructive POST.
